content: {"decision":"Reject as proposed; enforce authorization and validation before success.","risks":["Authentication alone does not establish tenant ownership or permission to create, fetch, or change policy for a workflow.","Caller-supplied fetch-time policies can weaken acceptance criteria after generation and bypass required validation.","A generator response is untrusted output; marking it succeeded immediately conflates generation completion with validated success.","Mutable policies and premature success can produce inconsistent reads and trigger downstream actions on invalid output."],"required_changes":["Enforce tenant-scoped resource authorization on creation, retrieval, policy selection, and asynchronous processing; bind each workflow and result to its tenant.","Resolve and persist an authorized, versioned policy at creation, with server-enforced minimum requirements that callers cannot weaken.","Validate policy configuration against an allowlisted, bounded schema; reject unauthorized overrides. Fetch-time options must not change canonical acceptance or status.","Persist generator output as pending validation; mark succeeded only after required structural and semantic checks pass. Represent generation and validation failures explicitly.","Make validation and status transitions atomic or concurrency-safe and idempotent; release downstream effects only after validated success. Record policy version and validation outcome."],"evidence_needed":["Authorization rules and negative tests for cross-tenant and unauthorized same-tenant workflow/result access, including workers and caches.","Policy contract and tests proving lenient, malformed, or unauthorized policies cannot bypass server requirements.","State-transition design and tests showing invalid output, validator errors, retries, and concurrent fetches cannot yield premature success or downstream effects.","Audit examples linking tenant, workflow, output, immutable policy version, validation outcome, and final status."]}
